title: Translating Whole Grain Guidance into U.S. Federal Nutrition Programs: Considerations for Increasing Intake and Maintaining Program Effectiveness
content: Background & Objectives: Whole grains are an important component of healthy dietary patterns, but intake in the U.S. population remains low. Federal nutrition programs can help address this gap through their broad coverage and reliance on meal pattern and nutrition standards based on the Dietary Guidelines for Americans (DGAs). The 2025–2030 DGAs continue to identify whole grains as part of a healthy dietary pattern, emphasizing fiber-rich whole grains, while prioritizing protein, recommending reductions in added sugars, and addressing the level of food processing. As a result of these new guidelines, the Cereals & Grains Association convened multiple stakeholders from across the food system to examine how changes to the DGAs may influence federal nutrition program standards and ultimately whole grain intake among the beneficiaries of these programs in the United States. Findings: Potential changes to program standards can improve the availability of whole grain foods and increase their whole grain content, but offering foods does not mean they will be consumed. Effective translation requires an integrated consideration of nutritional standards, operational feasibility, affordability, access, participant acceptance, and continuous improvement through monitoring and adjustment. Greater emphasis on protein and processing can complement whole grain guidance, but depending on implementation and communication, it could unintentionally reduce whole grain consumption. Dietary modeling, coordinated planning, realistic implementation timelines, and regular program evaluation can help predict and potentially avoid these consequences. Conclusions: Successful implementation of new nutritional standards should be assessed by meaningful increases in whole grain consumption while maintaining diet quality, affordability, participation, and program effectiveness.Significance and Novelty: This work integrates scientific evidence with multidisciplinary perspectives to identify practical considerations for translating whole grain guidance into federal nutrition programs.
